cells.B: Week 4: Research Preparation
Hello, Learners!

As we enter Week 4, we're focusing on qualitative research methods and their analytical processes. This week, you'll choose one of the major qualitative approaches—Case Study, Phenomenology, Delphi, or Grounded Theory—and explore its analytical process through the literature.
Steps to Prepare for This Week's Discussion and Assignment:
Choose Your Qualitative Approach:

Select one of the approved qualitative methods for your research: Case Study, Phenomenology, Delphi, or Grounded Theory. Think about your interests and how the chosen approach aligns with your research goals.
Conduct a Literature Search:

Begin your literature search by looking for seminal works that detail the analytical process for your chosen method. Key databases like Google Scholar, JSTOR, or your institution's library can be invaluable resources.
Pay particular attention to foundational texts and influential authors in the field. These works will provide you with a solid understanding of the methodology and its application.
Compare Terminology:

As you review the literature, take note of the specific terminology used in your chosen approach. For example, if you select Grounded Theory, familiarize yourself with concepts like "open coding," "axial coding," and "theoretical sampling."

Then, compare this terminology with that found in the Generic Thematic Analysis of Qualitative Data document. Identify any similarities or differences in the terms used, and consider how these terms reflect the methodologies' unique focuses.
Explore Underlying Assumptions:

Investigate the assumptions that underpin your chosen qualitative approach. For instance, phenomenology emphasizes understanding participants' lived experiences, while case studies focus on in-depth exploration of specific instances.
Contrast these assumptions with those associated with Generic Thematic Analysis. Consider how these foundational beliefs influence the research process and the interpretation of data.
Synthesize Your Findings:

As you gather information, synthesize your findings into a coherent understanding of your chosen approach. Be prepared to discuss how the analytical processes, terminology, and assumptions compare to those in Generic Thematic Analysis.
Prepare for Discussion:

Formulate your thoughts and insights based on your research. Think about how you can contribute to the discussion and what questions you might want to pose to your peers regarding their experiences with qualitative methodologies.

By following these steps, you will be well-prepared for this week’s discussion and assignment. Engaging deeply with the literature will enhance your understanding of qualitative research methods and their application in your own work.
Looking forward to an engaging week of exploration and discussion!
Spine-Tight Revision

This generic qualitative inquiry will establish methodological rigor through the trustworthiness criteria of credibility, dependability, confirmability, and transferability rather than through quantitative measures such as Cronbach’s alpha, which assesses the internal consistency of scale-based instruments (Lincoln & Guba, 1985). Potential threats include researcher bias when interpreting stakeholder salience through power, legitimacy, and urgency (PLU); inconsistent interview probing; participant recall and social-desirability bias; coercive recruitment conditions; inaccurate transcription; premature theme development; and insufficient corroboration of participant accounts. Credibility will be strengthened through purposive recruitment of qualified U.S. SME IT/network managers, a standardized semi-structured interview protocol with critical-incident prompts, transcript verification, negative-case analysis, and triangulation of participant accounts with available recovery plans, escalation procedures, test reports, and recoverability-assurance records. Dependability will be supported through consistent data-collection procedures and an audit trail documenting the progression from excerpts and meaning units to codes, categories, themes, and conclusions. Confirmability will be strengthened through reflexive journaling and documentation of theoretical and analytical decisions, particularly when PLU operates as a sensitizing framework. Transferability will be supported through contextual descriptions of U.S. SME conditions, ITDRPaaS arrangements, stakeholder relationships, decision rights, escalation pathways, evidence standards, and third-party dependencies, while pseudonyms, organizational masking, and data de-identification will protect confidentiality. Together, these procedures will provide a traceable and defensible basis for interpreting how stakeholder-salience dynamics shape the governance-to-assurance chain through which U.S. SMEs seek to produce and sustain recoverability assurance (Korstjens & Moser, 2018; Lincoln & Guba, 1985; Merriam & Tisdell, 2016; Nowell et al., 2017).
